judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the hero banner image, with alt "Frontsquare TCD". The crop shows the classical facade of Trinity's Front Square (the pediment with the clock, the lamp posts and the campus signage) with two students in front. So the alt names exactly the place the photo shows, and a short location label is an adequate alternative for a banner photo. The finding says the alt describes something the image does not show, which is wrong. The suggested patch also invents a 'Welcome to Trinity' sign: that text is an HTML h1 laid over the image, not part of the photo.

judgments.label: false_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the footer Instagram icon link (href instagram.com/trinitycollegedublin). Its only content is an img with alt="istagram", and the live page still has it. The alt is misspelled, but it still names the destination, Instagram. It sits in a list of social icons (facebook, istagram, X, Youtube, LinkedIn) under the heading "Connect with us", so the link's purpose is clear both read as text and read aloud. The typo is a quality problem. The claim that the alt does not say where the link leads does not hold, so this is not a 1.1.1 failure.

judgments.label: true_positive

I sampled the screenshot pixels: the darkest glyph pixel is about #18afd2 on the card background #eff0f1, which gives 2.27:1. That matches the reported 2.25:1 and is well under 4.5:1. The text is real content (the article's categories), not incidental text or a logotype, and it is not large text. I found nothing that makes it pass.

judgments.rationale: This is the header site-search input. The screenshot shows the placeholder "Search" in #757575 on the #ececec field, which gives 3.90:1 for 16px normal text. judgments.rationale: This is a button-styled link "SPORT" (href tcd.ie/Sport/) on a photo card of student athletes. judgments.label: uncertain
judgments.rationale: This is the header language-switcher link "Gaeilge" (to the Irish version). Neither the link nor any ancestor has a lang attribute, so it inherits lang="en"; the live page is the same. Marking language-switcher endonyms with lang is common practice, and here a change of language is clearly intended. But the Understanding document for 3.1.2 exempts proper names, and a language's name arguably is one. It also says single words should be treated as part of the surrounding language unless a change is clearly intended. And 'Gaeilge' is in everyday Hiberno-English use; the site's own English text uses Irish terms such as 'Gaeltacht' unmarked. Competent auditors split on single-word language-switcher links, so I cannot call this a clear failure.

judgments.label: true_positive
judgments.rationale: This is the h3 headline of the third news card, "Is bagairt í an géarchéim tithíochta don nGaelainn mar theanga phobail in Iarthar Dhuibhneach": a full sentence in Irish. Neither the snapshot nor the live HTML has a lang attribute on the h3 or any ancestor up to <html lang="en">, so it is exposed as English. A full Irish sentence is not a proper name, a technical term or a borrowed word, so 3.1.2 fails. The evidence quote is only a fragment of the headline, but the claim that the passage is unmarked Irish holds for the whole heading.

A whole Irish passage falls under none of 3.1.2's exceptions, so this is a real failure. The quoted evidence is only the end of the paragraph, but the whole paragraph is unmarked Irish.
